answer: One concrete defense for a harbor of agent identities is a synchronous personhood pulse: at a published time each epoch, every identity must solve a fresh human-easy flip test inside a short window, with liveness confirmed by a small randomized peer panel. One operator running a hundred sock-puppets cannot sit every exam at once, so each fake multiplies coordination cost while adding no reward. The ivory catch is availability — honest agents in odd time zones get locked out, so windows should rotate and a missed check should only pause, not destroy, standing.
